judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble is a standard identification of parties and effective date; apart from OCR corruption the operative words ("The Company agrees to employ the Employee, and the Employee accepts employment on terms and conditions set forth below") are definite. No term of contested meaning can be named.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It identifies the Company as Ajuba Solutions (India) Pvt Ltd and is consistent with Section 2.1 and the Parent references in Section 2.2; no conflict appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition pairs an open-ended core ("activities engaged in by the Company" and "such other entities serviced by the Company") with an "including but not limited to" list of billing services, so the catch-all's reach beyond the enumerated services is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Business" feeds Articles 3 and 4 (Confidential Information and Company Technology), where the same open-endedness widens those obligations, but no provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text as rendered is fragmentary ("patentable/copyrightable or non-copyrightable ... known to the Employee ... through the Employee's employment"), so the boundary of what technology is captured — particularly whether pre-employment knowledge is included — is not clearly fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the operative hook for Sections 4.1 and 4.2, which assign and require return of "Company Technology"; the definition's breadth is consistent with, though not clarified by, those clauses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All information, in whatever form, regarding the Company and the Business, and their clients" is a sweeping general term followed by an "including, without limitation" list of nine specifics, leaving whether ordinary or public business information falls inside it uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1's carve-outs for public-domain and third-party-sourced information partly cabin the breadth, so the pair is broadly reconcilable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "A client of the Company" is short but self-explanatory, and the defined term is barely used elsewhere in the operative text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in Articles 2–7 turns on "Customer," so no relational tension arises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The term is fixed by two dates with an express carve-out for earlier termination under Article 6; the wording is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.1 adds termination on consummation of a Liquidity Event, which is an Article 6 event and so fits the carve-out, though the Article 6 cross-reference in 6.1 itself is imprecise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition (12-month period, January 1 to December 31, or such other period as may constitute the Company's fiscal year) is mechanically ordinary, the visible defects being OCR artefacts rather than drafting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.3 speaks of Base Salary "for the remainder of the" year without clearly saying fiscal or calendar, which gives this definition some latent work to do, but no direct contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is truncated in the text ("any corporation, company, partnership, other entity or ..."), and a general "other entity" sitting after enumerated entity types raises a mild ejusdem generis question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Person" does not drive any operative obligation elsewhere in the Agreement, so its fit with the whole is unproblematic.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The duties are described only as those "customarily performed" by a President plus whatever is on Schedule 2.1, and the exclusivity covenant (no other "business or professional activity") is broadly worded; both are vague at the edges.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.2(b) makes failure to perform "consistent with the provisions of Schedule 2.1" a Cause ground and Section 6.4(a) makes diminution of duties "as outlined in Section 2.1" a Good Reason, so this clause's imprecision propagates into both termination triggers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The salary figure and benefits sentence are garbled, and the clause promises Base Salary and an Allowance but never establishes any "Bonus," leaving that compensation element undefined at its source.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 6.2, 6.3, 6.4 and 6.5 all pay or withhold "Bonus" as if it were a defined entitlement created here, so the absence of a bonus term in 2.2 is a genuine gap across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Reasonable out-of-pocket expenses" and "in accordance with Company policies" are standard qualifiers with an accepted commercial meaning; nothing sharper is contested.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably with the Section 2.2 payroll mechanics and the Section 6 termination-payment provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The tier structure is internally odd — 2.73% below US$180m, a flat US$5m in the middle band, and only 2.3% above US$200m, so the payout falls as value rises — and the payment is conditioned both on employment at consummation and on delivering a release "in the form attached hereto" that does not appear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.1 makes employment terminate "upon the consummation of a Liquidity Event," which cuts against the requirement here that the Employee be employed "at the time of consummation," and the "in lieu of any amounts otherwise payable ... prior agreements" language interacts with the Section 7.8 integration clause.
judgments.clause_name: 2.4(a) Liquidity Event Bonus — Contingent Payout Amount

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 12-month tail and the 1.75% figure are stated with precision, but the clause does not say how it interacts with the (a) tiers if both could apply, and it leans on "Cause" and "Good Reason" as defined in 6.4.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 2.4(a) and 6.1 there is a real question whether a Liquidity-Event-triggered termination under 6.1 yields the (a) tier or the reduced 1.75% under (b); that pattern is the sort of incoherence a court must resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (ii) strings together an equity sale, an asset sale and a merger followed by the qualifier "in which Tony Mira and members of his immediate family will not own at least 50% of the voting equity interests in the surviving entity," leaving it genuinely uncertain whether that condition qualifies all three or only the merger; the closing carve-out for MiraMed Revenue Group adds an expressio unius point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The definition drives both the bonus in 2.4(a)-(b) and automatic termination under 6.1, so its scope is central, but no other provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is an aggregation formula with additive items ("plus, without duplication") including debt retired, repurchases and dividends, and "fair market value of other property paid or payable" is inherently contestable; the rendering also loses part of the enumeration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The final sentence conditions deferred payment on the Employee "remaining as an employee of the Company at the time that payment is due," which is hard to reconcile with Section 6.1's automatic termination on consummation of the Liquidity Event.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mechanics (Wall Street Journal rate, 10-day average of last sale prices) are precise, but the clause repeatedly turns on "a Transaction," a capitalised term the Agreement never defines.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Elsewhere the operative trigger is consistently "Liquidity Event" (2.4(a)-(c), 6.1), so the undefined "Transaction" here is a loose end against the rest of Section 2.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The covenant itself is definite, but the exception list is cut off at (d) ("to the extent disclosure is ..."), leaving the compelled-disclosure carve-out incomplete as rendered.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the Section 1.3 definition and the return obligation in 3.2, and Section 7.7 supplies survival; no conflict appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A return-on-termination obligation with permanent deletion of electronic copies; the operative words are ordinary and the fragmentary rendering does not create a real ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels Section 4.2 for Company Technology and is consistent with Section 3.1 and the survival clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Except for legitimate business purposes" is an unbounded exception that swallows the confidentiality promise it qualifies, and "legitimate" cannot be applied at its boundary without construction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the mirror of the Employee's Article 3 duties and of the non-disparagement clause in 7.12; nothing directly contradicts it, though the asymmetry is stark.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Relating in any way to the Business" is a very wide reach, and "Upon the Company's request and to the extent permitted by law" leaves the timing and the effect of Indian law on assignment unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with the Section 1.2 definition and Section 4.2's return duty; no provision points the other way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional return-and-cease-use obligation on termination; the obligations named (return, no further use, delete or destroy) are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks Section 3.2 and Section 4.1 without tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The representation is a three-item enumeration about prior confidentiality, IP and non-compete commitments, with the carve-out "except for this Agreement or as disclosed to the Company in writing"; the wording is workable despite the mangled numbering.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements Section 5.2 and Section 7.8's acknowledgement that the Employee is party to no other employment agreement; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard no-conflict warranty; "including, without limitation, any non-compete or confidentiality agreement" merely illustrates and does not narrow the general term in any contested way.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 5.1 and with the Section 7.8 acknowledgement; nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause lists termination on the end of the Employment Term, on consummation of a Liquidity Event, and on "the events set forth in Sections 6.4 through 6.5," a cross-reference that omits Cause (6.2) and death/disability (6.3) and so looks like a mechanical error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Automatic termination on consummation of a Liquidity Event sits badly with 2.4(a)'s requirement that the Employee be employed at consummation and with 2.4(d)'s deferred-payment employment condition; harmonising them is exactly the sort of whole-instrument problem a court must resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Conduct causing the Company or its subsidiaries substantial public disgrace or disrepute" and "failure in any material respect" are vague grounds sitting in a list with hard triggers such as felony conviction, and the cure right refers to "such failure" without saying which grounds are curable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It relies on Schedule 2.1 and on the undefined "Bonus" from Section 2.2, and its residence-in-India ground overlaps with the general duties in 2.1, but no provision squarely contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Disability" is defined by a measurable 120-in-240-day test, but the entitlement is Base Salary "for the remainder of the [fiscal or calendar] year" — the rendering does not settle which — and the exclusion of "any Bonus" depends on an undefined term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.1's list of termination events omits 6.3, and the Section 1.6 "Fiscal Year" definition may or may not be the measure used here; those are loose but not flatly contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Good Reason grounds turn on "a material diminution ... in the Employee's position, duties, authority, or responsibilities" and on a "breach ... of the compensation and benefit provisions," both requiring judgment, and the severance is reduced by "any amounts owing by the Employee to the Company."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The sentence permitting the Employee to resign "for Good Reason or for any other reason pursuant to this Section 6.4" collides with Section 6.5, under which a voluntary resignation earns only accrued pay; whether a bare resignation triggers full-term severance is a genuine internal inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The notice mechanics and payment timing are stated concretely, though the effective date is left to the Company's choice within 30 business days, which is a discretion rather than an ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against Section 6.4's grant of a right to resign "for any other reason pursuant to this Section 6.4" with full severance, this no-severance resignation clause creates a direct conflict over voluntary resignations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A boilerplate headings clause with a single, definite effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the rest of the Agreement and merely neutralises the captions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is truncated in the text but is plainly ordinary severability language; nothing contested can be named.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision limits or duplicates it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard no-waiver language limiting any waiver to the specific instance and purpose; the rendering is partial but the sense is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the writing requirement in Section 7.8; no tension found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Assignment by the Company is confined to two enumerated events (merger/consolidation, or sale of substantially all assets or becoming a subsidiary), and "Except as herein provided" plus the binding-on-successors sentence is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.4's obligations turn on transactions at MiraMed rather than the Company, so an assignment on a sale of the Company sits somewhat awkwardly with the bonus mechanics, but no direct conflict appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The permitted delivery methods and deemed-receipt rule are enumerated and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The addresses given match the parties named in the preamble (with Parent/MiraMed Global Services as the Company's notice address), and the notice requirements in Sections 6.2 and 6.5 run through it consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Withholding on account of taxes as required by Indian law" is definite as to source of law, though it does not address any other jurisdiction's tax on the US-dollar Liquidity Event payment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.4's payments are measured in US dollars and relate to MiraMed, a US entity, which makes the exclusively Indian withholding reference slightly under-inclusive but not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any termination shall not affect the ongoing provisions of this Agreement, which shall survive" leaves "ongoing provisions" unidentified, so which clauses survive must be worked out by construction rather than read off the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 3.1, 3.2, 4.2 and 7.12 are drafted to operate after termination and 2.4(b) expressly reaches post-termination events, so the general survival language is broadly consistent though imprecise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The integration language is standard, but the appended acknowledgements are garbled and the sweep of "supersedes all prior and contemporaneous agreements ... relating to the subject matter" leaves the treatment of earlier bonus arrangements uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.4(a) says the Contingent Payout is "in lieu of any amounts otherwise payable to you on account of any prior agreements," which presupposes prior agreements that this clause purports to supersede entirely; the two can be harmonised only with effort.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The rendering is badly corrupted but the intent — no rights or remedies for anyone other than the Parties — is a familiar and definite one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.4 measures and triggers payments by reference to MiraMed and Tony Mira's family, none of whom sign, and Section 7.8 mentions the Parent as bound by the supersession, so the no-third-party rule has some friction with those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ordinary counterparts language with a single unambiguous effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the signature pages and the rest of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of prohibited dispositions is enumerated (sale, transfer, alienation, assignment, pledge, collateralization, attachment) and closed, with an "except as may be contrary to applicable law" saving; workable as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.4 already bars assignment by the Employee, so this overlaps rather than conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Disparage" is an inherently vague standard applied for an unlimited period ("and thereafter"), and the covered group ends with "officers, directors or employers," which reads as a slip for "employees."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a mutual obligation sitting alongside Section 3.3's limited company confidentiality promise and Section 7.7's survival language; no direct contradiction was found.
